parsed.main_gap: Lemma 4 asserts that |E|<|V| forces the pairing multigraph to have no cycle and no loop; this is false (a disconnected graph can have a cyclic/looped component). The component of vertex n need not be a tree.

errors.description: The claim that a multigraph with fewer edges than vertices has no cycles or loops is false: e.g. pieces 8u,4u,2u,u with 8u cut into 5u,3u gives the top pair {5u,3u} as a loop at vertex n. So the component T containing n may fail to be a tree and the proper 2-colouring argument breaks as written. Correct fact: some component is a tree; since (3.1) holds for every nonempty J, choosing that component repairs the proof, but this is not what is written.
errors.quote: Since $|E|<|V|$, the multigraph $G$ contains no cycle and no loop: a cycle or a loop through $v$ vertices already uses at least $v$ edges, so a graph containing one would have at least as many edges as vertices, forcing $|E|\ge|V|$ — impossible.

parsed.notes: Answer 2^n/(2^{n+1}-1) is correct. Lemma 2 (greedy picking value), the signed-sum property (3.1), and the upper-bound construction (subset-sum pigeonhole + cross-pairing cuts, mark count ≤ n, distinctness) are all carefully and correctly argued. The only defect is the false graph-theoretic claim in the lower-bound lemma; the repair is short but not supplied.
